transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Former President Barack Obama campaigned in Ohio and Michigan yesterday,
rallying Democrats ahead of next week's midterm elections.
In Detroit, Obama threw his support behind U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed.
Michigan Public Radio's Colin Jackson reports.
Obama's speech came as Michigan Democrats try to lock down their base
on the first day of statewide early in-person voting.
Republicans have tried to paint El-Sayed, who was born and raised in Michigan,
as caring more about Arab countries than Michigan communities.
Obama says that playbook sounds familiar.
They may even use your name or your faith to sound.
I suggest that you are dangerous and less than trustworthy
and less patriotic and less American than they are.
We have seen this movie before as starred in it.
Democrats and Republicans see Michigan as must-win on the path to a U.S. Senate majority.
President Donald Trump is also campaigning on Michigan this weekend.
For NPR News, I'm Colin Jackson.
More than 400,000 people took to the streets across France on Saturday,
protesting everything from crumbling schools to the high cost of living.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports from Paris.
Protesters of all ages and backgrounds coursed down a Paris boulevard.
Students, workers, parents, retirees, and yellow vests,
the largely white working-class movement that bedeviled
French President Emmanuel Macron in his first term.
These left-wing demonstrators held placards calling to tax the rich
and for Macron to resign.
Dimitri Knoll explains why there is such anger.
We hate Macron, he says, because he's been leading these ultra-capitalist policies
for 10 years that are just widening inequalities,
and young people have less hope for the future.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley.
Stock markets have had an impressive run over the past four years,
providing a big boost to investors and many retirement funds.
But as NPR's Rafael Nam reports,
there are growing concerns about whether those gains can last.
By the numbers, stocks appear in good shape.
All three major indexes are headed for decent gains this year.
But it's been a volatile ride, as a lot of uncertainty is building up.
There's the war with Iran, which is leading to a surge in energy prices.
The Federal Reserve is raising interest rates,
and concerns remain about AI stocks,
which are becoming a critical part of markets and the broader economy.
Just this week, META said it would have to raise even more money for AI,
raising concerns about how much money is being invested in the sector.
So analysts are cautioning, brace yourself, because it could be a bumpy ride.
Rafael Nam, NPR News.
This is NPR News in Washington.
The Archdiocese of New York has agreed to an $800 million settlement
with about 1,300 people who say clergy sexually abused them.
It's the second-largest settlement involving a Catholic archdiocese in the United States
behind the $880 million Los Angeles agreed to pay in 2024.
Attorneys for survivors call it a powerful moment in their pursuit of justice.
The Milwaukee Brewers have taken a two-games-to-none lead in the World Series
after beating the Tampa Bay Rays 5-4 last night.
Steve Futterman reports it was a come-from-behind victory.
Before the Milwaukee Brewers came to bat for the first time last night,
they already trailed Tampa Bay 4-0.
It didn't phase the Brewers.
They began to slowly chip away, getting two runs in the bottom of the first,
then single runs in the fourth and sixth that tied the score at 4-4.
In the seventh, Milwaukee took the lead on a single from Cooper Pratt.
Was Pratt nervous? You better believe it.
I mean, heart was racing. I'm not going to lie.
You try and relax and calm down and breathe.
Historically, teams that win the first two games go on to win the series
more than 80 percent of the time.
Sunday is a travel day.
The series resumes on Monday in Tampa Bay with Game 3.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Futterman at the World Series in Milwaukee.
I'm Windsor Johnston, and you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
in PR.

topics.text: Former President Obama rallies in Detroit for Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed ahead of midterms
Over 400,000 protest across France against crumbling schools and high cost of living
Stock markets face growing concerns over Iran war, Fed rate hikes, and AI investment
Archdiocese of New York agrees to $800 million settlement with about 1,300 abuse survivors
Milwaukee Brewers take 2-0 World Series lead over Tampa Bay Rays with 5-4 comeback win
